title: Bought a home in Vero Beach this year? How to file for homestead before March 1
seoTitle: Vero Beach Homestead Exemption: Who Qualifies, How to File
description: A plain guide to the Florida homestead exemption for Vero Beach homeowners: who qualifies, the Jan. 1 and March 1 dates, the 3% cap and where to file.
dek: Homestead is one of Florida's biggest property tax breaks for homeowners, and you have to ask for it. Here is who qualifies, the two dates that matter, and where to file in Indian River County.
facebook: New to your Vero Beach home? Your tax bill won't shrink on its own. Florida's homestead exemption can take up to $50,000 off your home's taxable value, but you have to file. Here's who qualifies, the Jan. 1 and March 1 dates, and where to apply.
keywords: Indian River County homestead exemption how to file
Save Our Homes 3% cap Indian River County
Indian River County Property Appraiser homestead

body.text: Property tax bills arrive this fall. If you bought your Vero Beach home this year, your first bill is a good reminder of something easy to miss: the homestead exemption does not happen by itself. You have to apply.
Here is how it works, in plain English.

body.title: The short version
body.text: If you own your home and it is your permanent residence on Jan. 1, you can file for homestead with the Indian River County Property Appraiser. The deadline is March 1. File now and it counts for the 2027 tax year, as long as you live there on Jan. 1, 2027. You can apply online or at the Vero Beach office, 1800 27th St., Building B, 772-226-1469.
What homestead takes off your taxes
According to the Florida Department of Revenue, the homestead exemption can take up to $50,000 off your home's assessed value. It comes in two parts:

items: The first $25,000 applies to all property taxes, including school taxes.
A second exemption of up to $25,000 applies to assessed value over $50,000. It only applies to non-school taxes.
That second $25,000 is adjusted each Jan. 1 for inflation, but only when inflation goes up. It never goes down.

body.text: So a home with a lower assessed value may not get the full second part. The Property Appraiser figures that out for you.
The bigger long-term win: the 3% cap

Homestead also turns on a cap called Save Our Homes. Once your home has homestead, its assessed value can go up each year by no more than 3%, or the change in the Consumer Price Index if that is lower. That is true even when market values jump.

Over years, that gap between market value and assessed value can grow large. The Property Appraiser notes that when a home is sold or changes ownership, the value goes back to market value. The new owner then applies for their own homestead.
Moving from another Florida home that had homestead? You may be able to bring part or all of that built-up savings with you. This is called portability. Ask about it when you file.

items: You own the home, and it is your permanent residence, or the permanent residence of someone who depends on you.
You live there on Jan. 1 of the tax year. The Property Appraiser's site says permanent Florida residency is required on Jan. 1.
You file by March 1 of that same year.

body.text: The state's brochure also says you can lose the exemption if you rent out the home, if it stops being your permanent home, or if you are no longer a permanent Florida resident. If you are thinking about renting your place, ask the Property Appraiser first.

The state form is called DR-501. The Department of Revenue says first-time filers should be ready to answer who was on the title on Jan. 1, whether you lived there on Jan. 1, and whether you claim residency anywhere else. You will also need Social Security numbers for the applicants.
The Property Appraiser may ask for proof that this is your permanent home. Items the state lists include:

items: A Florida driver license or Florida ID card.
The address on your last IRS return.
Bank statements or proof of paying utilities at the home.

body.text: A note on the Nov. 3 ballot

Amendment 3 on the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot would change the homestead exemption if voters approve it. According to the Manatee County Property Appraiser's FAQ, it would raise the non-school exemption to up to $150,000 starting Jan. 1, 2027, and up to $250,000 starting Jan. 1, 2028. The $25,000 school exemption would not change. It needs at least 60% of the vote to pass. Either way, you still need homestead on file to get any of it. The rules in this article are the rules in effect today.

items: Look at your tax bill or look up your parcel on the Indian River County Property Appraiser's website. Check whether a homestead exemption is listed.

Not there and you live in the home full time? Plan to file. Use the online homestead application on ircpa.org, or go to the Vero Beach office at 1800 27th St., Building B. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
Gather your Florida driver license, vehicle tag number and a utility bill before you start. It goes faster.
Mark two dates on your calendar: live there by Jan. 1, file by March 1.
Coming from another Florida homestead? Ask about portability when you file.
Watch your mailbox. The Property Appraiser's site warns owners about a mailer advertisement. You can file directly with the Property Appraiser yourself.

faq.q: When is the homestead exemption deadline in Indian River County?
faq.a: March 1. You must own the home and make it your permanent residence by Jan. 1 of the tax year, then file with the Indian River County Property Appraiser by March 1 of that year.

faq.q: How much does homestead save in Florida?
faq.a: It can take up to $50,000 off your home's assessed value. The first $25,000 applies to all property taxes, including school taxes. A second exemption of up to $25,000 applies to assessed value over $50,000 for non-school taxes and is adjusted for inflation.

faq.q: Can I file for homestead online in Indian River County?
faq.a: Yes. The Indian River County Property Appraiser offers an online homestead application on ircpa.org. You can also apply in person at the Vero Beach office, 1800 27th St., Building B, or the Sebastian office, 1921 U.S. 1.

faq.q: I bought my house in 2026. When does my homestead start?
faq.a: If it is your permanent home on Jan. 1, 2027, and you file by March 1, 2027, the exemption applies to the 2027 tax year. The Property Appraiser's site says applications filed now are for the 2027 tax year.

faq.q: What is the Save Our Homes cap?
faq.a: Once your home has homestead, its assessed value can rise each year by no more than 3% or the change in the Consumer Price Index, whichever is lower. When the home is sold, the value resets to market value.
